description: §17.1 the PRESENT half for a wiring-bearing if= subtree, and the part absence alone cannot prove: after the flip the subtree must not only exist, its OWN wiring must be live. A click flips @open false->true; #panel mounts, the ${@label} interpolation renders "alpha" (so the descendant display effect was bound at mount time, not at boot when the subtree was inert <template> content), and typing into the bind:value input writes @typed (so the two-way binding was re-bound too — that wiring is emitted once at file scope against a document that cannot see into a <template>, and would otherwise be permanently dead for a mounted subtree).
rationale: §17.1 a true if= renders the element. §5.4 bind:value is two-way on a form control. Under mount/unmount the subtree's wiring is created per mount cycle rather than once at boot, so this case is the one that fails if the mount path forgets to re-bind: absence tests pass either way, and an emit-shape test cannot tell a bound listener from an unbound one.
